Mia (product): quick q — for autofallbacks can we guarantee a stable event_id per decision so audits can link a fallback to the original request?
Ryan (eng): yes we emit a decision_id currently but it's ephemeral per request, not always in logs.
Sam (platform): ephemerality is the problem. We need a canonical id that surfaces in runtime, routing logs, and the console playback.
Anya (sre): +1. When incidents hit we keep asking: which requests were downgraded, which rule triggered, and which model handled the fallback. Hard to correlate.
Jordan (analytics): for dashboards we also need the trigger type (latency/error/ccap) and the exact policy snapshot id used. Right now we only get a string like "fallback_v3".
Mia (product): proposal: attach three fields to every decision: canonical_event_id (uuid), policy_snapshot_id (sha-ish), trigger_reason (enum).
Ryan (eng): that's reasonable. canonical_event_id must be generated at the first policy evaluation so it survives retries and retries don't produce new ids.
Sam (platform): implementation notes: generator at the routing layer, add to the response headers and to internal trace. Example header: `X-Rdw-Decision-Id: 8f14e45f-e1b2-4c6a`
Leo (design): console UX ask — show a compact "decision trail" row with event id + expand to show timeline: evaluate -> fallback -> model chosen -> audit link.
Anya (sre): we also need a dropdown to replay the exact policy_snapshot used in case the policy changed. Replay must be deterministic.
Jordan (analytics): policy_snapshot_id must be immutable and stored with the policy change event in the config store; the analytics pipeline will join on that id.
Mia (product): what about privacy: do we include any request-level tokens in the decision logs? we should avoid any PII.
Ryan (eng): canonical_event_id is OK (opaque uuid). We should strip prompt text from the fallback audit view by default and make full payloads gated behind perms.
Sam (platform): telemetry impact: adding three small fields is ~5 bytes per event but multiplied by QPS could be significant. We should sample for high-volume routes but always record full traces for errors.
Anya (sre): sampling is tricky for compliance. For customers with retention/SLA needs we should have option to force-store all events.
Jordan (analytics): agreed, make sampling policy configurable per-route and per-customer tier. We'll surface sampling rate in the console.
Mia (product): UX acceptance criteria: 1) event id visible in trace and request logs; 2) console can filter by event id; 3) policy snapshot link opens snapshot view; 4) replayable in CI/sandbox.
Leo (design): mock for decision-trail card incoming — will post in #design later.
Ryan (eng): action items: i) spec API header + internal trace field ii) add policy_snapshot_id to config-store write path iii) telemetry schema change iv) console filter + replay endpoint.
Sam (platform): I'll draft telemetry schema PR. Need to decide retention defaults and per-customer overrides.
Anya (sre): add ops runbook note: how to find all requests for an event id across regions (we need a cross-region index).
Mia (product): thanks — can we sync tomorrow 10am? aim to have a minimal MVP that covers auditability for enterprise customers.
